title: Key incident list — /ct/incident-{date}.json
description:
The public list a signing key's compromise publishes: the keys it concerns, the exposure window each was enumerated over, and every transparency-log entry inside that window found FORGED, signed with the key and never issued by the Association (FS08-104, CERT-023; FS-00 §6.2's amendment note of 2026-09-01 reserves the path). A relying party holding a token signed by a compromised key before its `notAfter` is told by every public verifier that the token's date is the signer's own claim (`key_compromised_before`); this list is where it checks: the SHA-256 of the token's compact JWS is the hash the log states for it, and a hash listed here was never issued.

WHAT IS FORGED. The key-compromise procedure (RB-04 steps 3 and 6) re-verifies the log against the Association's issuance records for each key's exposure window. A log entry in the window whose hash matches no issuance record was signed with the key and never issued, and it is listed here by its position in the log (`seq`) and its hash (`h`), in log order. An issuance record whose hash is missing from the log is a different failure, a broken log-before-deliver step, investigated and never listed here. An enumeration that found nothing is published too, with `forged` empty: it is the honest answer. Genuine certificates from the window are reissued under new ids with supersede links (`key-compromise-reissue`), which the log and the certificate records carry; this list does not.

THE KEYS AND THEIR WINDOWS. Each key the incident concerns is named by its `kid` with the exposure window its enumeration covered: from the earliest moment someone else may have held the key (`from`) to its containment (`until`). In the key set (`jwks.v1`) the key is then `compromised`, its `notAfter` is the earlier of its retirement and `from`, and its `psn:incidents` names this list by its path. A sandbox key is never named: sandbox signatures never enter the log (FS08-103).

FINAL ONCE PUBLISHED. A list never changes, so the edge may cache it as it caches a closed log segment. `{date}` in the path is `date`, the UTC date of `generatedAt`, the instant the incident was recorded, and not the plane's: every render writes the same bytes. A date names one list; anything found after a list was published is published as a list of its own, on a later date. Nothing in a list names a person: a log entry carries a family and a hash, never a subject, and so does this list.

x-psn.phase: P-M3 (producer: `jobs.index-build`, from an incident recorded by the key-compromise procedure). Nothing is published under this contract yet: no key has been compromised, nothing emits the path, and the edge does not route it yet.
x-psn.artifactPath: /ct/incident-{date}.json — one per recorded incident, final once published
x-psn.producer: `jobs.index-build` (P-M3), from an append-only record the key-compromise procedure writes (RB-04 step 6); a sample plane's builder may render a labelled one
consumers: relying parties holding a token signed by a compromised key
the /verify page's warning on such a token
independent auditors re-running the enumeration against the log
fsRefs: FS-08 §11 (FS08-104) and its dated note of 2026-09-26

generatedAt.description: The instant the incident was recorded, after its enumeration: the document's own instant, not the plane's, so every render writes the same bytes. Its UTC date is `date`.

source.description: Which plane produced this list. `sample` and `fixture` declare a NON-PRODUCTION plane: every page that renders it is labelled sample, and a production deployment refuses to serve it. `platform` is the producer of record, the platform database rendered by `jobs.index-build`. Required: a list of forged hashes from a synthetic plane must never pass for a production one. The curated registry never recorded an incident, so `registry-v0` is not admitted.

date.description: The `{date}` of the list's path, `/ct/incident-{date}.json`: the UTC date of `generatedAt`. A date names one list.

keys.description: Every key the incident concerns, each once, in `kid` order.

forged.description: Every log entry inside a listed key's exposure window whose hash matches no issuance record, each once, in log order (`seq` ascending). Empty when the enumeration found none.

kid.description: The compromised key, as the key set names it. Never a sandbox key: sandbox signatures never enter the log.

exposure.description: The exposure window the incident declared for this key and its enumeration covered: the instants every step of the procedure is scoped by.

from.description: The earliest moment someone else may have held the key. The key set's `notAfter` for the key is the earlier of its retirement and this instant.

until.description: The key's containment: the instant its vault version was disabled, after which it signs nothing. Later than `from`, and not later than `generatedAt`.

seq.description: The entry's global sequence number in the transparency log (`ct-segment.v1`), so an auditor finds it in its segment.

h.description: The entry's hash as the log states it: for a signed token, the SHA-256 of its compact JWS (CERT-030). A relying party computes it over the token it holds and looks for it here.
